findings.text: The opening paragraph says plainly what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. A newcomer can say what it is and why it matters after reading only the first paragraph.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page lives at Athena's address, but its title is about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer may think they are on the wrong site until the third paragraph says "This page is that study of firstmate."
findings.source: Page title and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The second section on the page is a broken demo. It shows an error where the evidence should be. This undercuts the claim made just above it that Athena records the models, verdict and cost for each job.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This link is meant for the project owner, yet it sits in the newcomer's header next to the main call to action. It means nothing to a first-time reader and competes with the "Next step" link.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: prerequisites, the clone command, ./setup.sh, and a first command to try. The early "Next step" link in the header jumps straight to them.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The page never says whether the reader needs an AI account or API key, what running a job costs, or which operating systems are supported. A newcomer would want to know these things before installing.
findings.source: Next steps: "either Claude Code or npm (to install Claude Code)"; lede: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it"

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed study of firstmate's internals, such as the exit-75 deferral and the places-held counter. It shows Athena's traceable style, but a newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to scroll past many screens of material they did not ask for.
findings.source: Sections "States of a piece of work", "Counters", "Transitions", "Why it is built this way", "Claims and sources"

findings.text: The study itself is well built for a reader. Terms are defined before they are used, and every statement links to a claim with file-and-line sources at a fixed commit. This shows the accountability the lede promises.
findings.source: Start here: "The three parts below say what firstmate is, follow one piece of work, and say what happens when something fails or has no limit."
